title: How did a 7.5 kW spark become 50 MW ships?

segments.text: How did a 7.5 kW spark become 50 MW ships?
In 1884 Charles Parsons built a reaction turbine that generated 7.5 kW (10.1 hp) of electricity.
He licensed the patent and George Westinghouse quickly enlarged the design.
The Parsons turbine proved easy to scale up, and the size of generators grew from the first 7.5 kW unit to units of 50,000 kW capacity during Parsons’ lifetime.
This dramatic increase helped power marine propulsion by the mid‑1880s and marked the start of large‑scale turbine power.
